STDO 3.0.3

STDO 3.0.3 is a normal, immutable `stable-v1` release. It bundles the project
representation tools and offline documentation with the methodology.

The installed documentation home now provides:

- **Constraints:** the historical STDO representation, with unified 3D, 2D and
  layered views and file-to-logical navigation.
- **Code example:** the reviewed ABIogenesis example, connecting selected
  requirements, code observations, proposed traces and test sources.
- **Lean proofs:** searchable declarations, exact proof source, readable
  explanations and the retained check report, with source-reference navigation.
- **Tools:** the pinned a_c and Codex/Claude Skills source bundle, with an
  integrity checker and explicit extraction into a separate writable workspace.

These readers are self-contained HTML pages; opening the installed pages needs
no web service or toolchain setup.

## Install and open the documentation

With STDO manager 0.1.6 already available:

```sh
stdo install v3.0.3 --repository https://github.com/foolishimp/specification_methodology.git --manifest-sha256 f07e6681355023e30ad8cc4c2ebecaa520ee4e75da6e140ef5a160b31082178d
stdo verify v3.0.3 --manifest-sha256 f07e6681355023e30ad8cc4c2ebecaa520ee4e75da6e140ef5a160b31082178d
stdo resolve stdo://releases/v3.0.3/standards/documentation/index.html
```

Open the absolute `path` returned by the last command in your browser. To
prepare a workspace-local manager with Python 3.11 or later, download the
[manager wheel](https://github.com/foolishimp/specification_methodology/releases/download/specification_methodology/v3.0.3/stdo_toolchain-0.1.6-py3-none-any.whl)
and its checksum from this release, then run:

```sh
python3 -m venv .stdo-manager
.stdo-manager/bin/python -m pip install ./stdo_toolchain-0.1.6-py3-none-any.whl
.stdo-manager/bin/stdo --store ./.stdo-store install v3.0.3 --repository https://github.com/foolishimp/specification_methodology.git --manifest-sha256 f07e6681355023e30ad8cc4c2ebecaa520ee4e75da6e140ef5a160b31082178d
.stdo-manager/bin/stdo --store ./.stdo-store resolve stdo://releases/v3.0.3/standards/documentation/index.html
```

The [installed-tooling guide at the immutable native commit](https://github.com/foolishimp/specification_methodology/blob/07bdb34a2d472a3b5e678f60584fd02b24a388f4/specification_methodology/v3/standards/tooling/README.md)
explains checked extraction, representation/code commands, optional Graphify
dependencies, Lean support and Skills installation. Extraction preserves the
installed release; it does not install dependencies or adopt a methodology
for an existing project.

## Exact release and scope

- Native commit: `07bdb34a2d472a3b5e678f60584fd02b24a388f4`.
- Annotated tag: `specification_methodology/v3.0.3`.
- Manifest SHA-256: `f07e6681355023e30ad8cc4c2ebecaa520ee4e75da6e140ef5a160b31082178d`.
- Native payload: 106 files; installation adds the manifest as its 107th file.
- Tool source bundle: 191 exact files from `9c9626ffd20ea88a75ac8143802c13f4f828ec1c`.

The four downloadable assets are the canonical manifest, manager wheel and
their checksum sidecars. Documentation and tool sources are inside the native
installation; no separate representation supplement is required.

The tools are distributed as source. Optional Python/parser/Graphify support,
Lean/Mathlib and compiled proof support require explicit setup in a writable
workspace. The proof reader retains an exact historical check—46 projection
outputs, 46 budget refusals and 204 audited declaration contracts—not a fresh
proof run or proof of application-code correctness. The code example's trace
links are proposals; test sources do not imply executed test results.

Independent review and installed-path checks cover the bounded distribution
and tooling behavior. Browser/WebGL visual qualification, fresh-machine Lean
execution, new coding-host Skills trials, semantic completeness and practical
efficiency retain their recorded limits. Existing a_c/Skills construction
bases and consumer installations are unchanged by this release.

body":"# STDO 3.0.2

STDO 3.0.2 is a published immutable release with no RC suffix. It adds recursive
Product composition, explicit edge authority and context conditions, composition
contracts and examples, and source-matched reference frames. The stable-v1 release
profile gives this exact version an immutable tag while preserving historical
RC release and selector semantics.

The accompanying manager 0.1.6 wheel supports stable acquisition and explicit
composition-edge verification. The updated a_c and Codex/Claude Skills sources are
checkpointed on main; those independently owned tools and their consumer bases
retain their own lifecycle. Installing the native method does not adopt a project
or change an existing method installation.

## Exact release

| Coordinate | Identity |
|---|---|
| Immutable tag | `specification_methodology/v3.0.2` |
| Native commit C | `23ca9c0929d7be8570edafaf30542e3daeb8dc1f` |

| Reviewed source A | `44448b14ecc9c5636d0e7972c7a4f1a80a07c623` |

The native distribution contains 86 payload files plus its installed manifest:
standards, generated frames, the supplied spec plugin, licence and release note.
The native predecessor is the published 3.0.1 RC1 commit; its tags and bytes remain
unchanged. No legacy 2.* coordinated cohort is republished.

## Install the exact method

Use Python 3.11 or later. Download the manager wheel, native manifest and their
checksum sidecars from the assets below. In that download directory, verify and create a separate environment:

```sh
shasum -a 256 -c stdo_toolchain-0.1.6-py3-none-any.whl.sha256
shasum -a 256 -c stdo-v3.0.2-manifest.json.sha256
python3 -m venv .stdo302
.stdo302/bin/python -I -m pip install ./stdo_toolchain-0.1.6-py3-none-any.whl
.stdo302/bin/python -I -m stdo_toolchain.cli --store ./stdo-store install v3.0.2 \
  --repository https://github.com/foolishimp/specification_methodology.git \
  --manifest-sha256 f7f3f824ee1ac3e048d1b1ea86ce3aae84866e2e9d5010fe5eda2e38e12f4477
.stdo302/bin/python -I -m stdo_toolchain.cli --store ./stdo-store verify v3.0.2 \
  --manifest-sha256 f7f3f824ee1ac3e048d1b1ea86ce3aae84866e2e9d5010fe5eda2e38e12f4477
```

The manager wheel is a separate distribution asset, not executable content added
to the native standards package. Existing installed 3.0.1/2.5.1 and pinned project
bases remain unchanged by this separate-store installation.

## Representation and evidence

The separate `stdo-v3.0.2-composition-release-supplement.tar.gz` and its sidecar bind
the same native commit and manifest. The archive supplies 32 authored composition
and release records, exact source custody, both graph carriers, and a portable
verifier. Check the sidecar, extract the archive, then run:

```sh
python3 -I -S -B stdo-v3.0.2-supplement/supplement.py verify \
  --bundle stdo-v3.0.2-supplement
```

Independent source and local-native readbacks passed. The exact manager wheel
passed 121 affected tests; a_c support passed 240 tests. Fresh isolated local
installation and both carrier recoveries passed on these exact assets. The
supplement is bounded to the selected 32 records; it does not complete the earlier
whole-method representation. Whole-method practical qualification, host behavior
and cost/efficiency claims remain outside this release's established evidence.

### Universal Reference Frame Method

`REFERENCE_FRAME_METHOD.md` introduces the finite engagement atom above any one
specification methodology or domain realization.

A frame binds one evaluation family to an exact workspace and topology basis,
material-relation manifold, coordinates and equality law, inherited invariants,
semantic/evaluation/decision authorities and operation authority where
material, admissible evidence, exclusions, closed result algebra, actor
capability envelope, declared dependencies, and invalidation conditions.

The method separately defines:

- frame-set declaration;
- exact activation;
- evaluation and closed result return;
- independently activated co-evaluation, assurance independence, and result
  conjunction;
- evidence or coordinate translation;
- material composition where an evaluation requires it;
- tuple-relative operational coverage with explicit residual uncertainty; and
- empirical revision after failures, topology mutation, evidence change, or
  capability change.

Frames need not form a hierarchy, partition, tree, service topology, or runtime
ontology. They may be disjoint or overlapping, refine, restrict, translate,
compose, or succeed one another. Structural disjointness, separately activated
evaluation, and assurance independence remain distinct. Role, persona, actor,
abstraction, component, and lens remain distinct from a frame; each may help
construct or activate one but does not become one by label.

The method explicitly admits `satisfied`, `falsified`, `indeterminate`,
`out_of_frame`, and `invalid_basis`. Operational full coverage is relative to
one declared workspace, outcome, basis, evaluation inventory, frame set, and
time. It does not assert that no undiscovered material evaluation exists.

Method self-qualification covers every claimed function and failure relation:
declaration, activation, evaluation, conjunction, translation, coverage,
revision, result consumption, material composition, authority conservation,
activation refusal, and the closed Worker-result mapping.

### Applied STDO Executive, Worker, And Reviewer Baseline

`STDO_REFERENCE_FRAME_BASELINE.md` is an optional derived application profile,
not a second execution constitution. It maps three overlapping finite
engagement frames onto existing STDO owners:

```text
Executive attempts Worker activation
  -> activation refusal returns to Executive and creates no Worker result
  -> after lawful activation, Worker returns
     candidate_ready | refused | incomplete | re_entry_requested to Executive
  -> Executive disposes directly when independent review is not required
     or activates Reviewer when it is required
  -> Reviewer independently reacquires and evaluates the exact subject
     and returns one Reference Frame Method result to Executive
  -> Executive applies the existing STDO disposition and continuation relation
```

The Worker carries only its inherited construction/transformation operation
authority and cannot admit, publish, accept itself, or activate the Reviewer.
The Reviewer cannot implement repair, return or apply an STDO disposition, or
select continuation. The Executive does not gain universal semantic,
operation, or implementation authority. Frames and actors are separately bound;
the profile requires no fixed actor count.

Projects may adopt the baseline or define another frame configuration through
existing Goals, Product, requirement, or accepted-design authority. A local
axioms carrier projects that authority and does not mint a parallel
constitutional layer.

STDO 3.0.3 is a normal, immutable `stable-v1` release. It bundles the project
representation tools and offline documentation with the methodology.

The installed documentation home now provides:

- **Constraints:** the historical STDO representation, with unified 3D, 2D and

STDO 3.0.2

STDO 3.0.2 is a published immutable release with no RC suffix. It adds recursive
Product composition, explicit edge authority and context conditions, composition
contracts and examples, and source-matched reference frames. The stable-v1 release
profile gives this exact version an immutable tag while preserving historical
RC release and selector semantics.

The accompanying manager 0.1.6 wheel supports stable acquisition and explicit
composition-edge verification. The updated a_c and Codex/Claude Skills sources are
checkpointed on main; those independently owned tools and their consumer bases
retain their own lifecycle. Installing the native method does not adopt a project
or change an existing method installation.

## Exact release

## Install the exact method

Use Python 3.11 or later. Download the manager wheel, native manifest and their
checksum sidecars from the assets below. In that download directory, verify and create a separate environment:

```sh
shasum -a 256 -c stdo_toolchain-0.1.6-py3-none-any.whl.sha256
shasum -a 256 -c stdo-v3.0.2-manifest.json.sha256
python3 -m venv .stdo302
.stdo302/bin/python -I -m pip install ./stdo_toolchain-0.1.6-py3-none-any.whl
.stdo302/bin/python -I -m stdo_toolchain.cli --store ./stdo-store install v3.0.2 \
  --repository https://github.com/foolishimp/specification_methodology.git \
  --manifest-sha256 f7f3f824ee1ac3e048d1b1ea86ce3aae84866e2e9d5010fe5eda2e38e12f4477

  --manifest-sha256 f7f3f824ee1ac3e048d1b1ea86ce3aae84866e2e9d5010fe5eda2e38e12f4477
```

The manager wheel is a separate distribution asset, not executable content added
to the native standards package. Existing installed 3.0.1/2.5.1 and pinned project
bases remain unchanged by this separate-store installation.

## Representation and evidence

The separate `stdo-v3.0.2-composition-release-supplement.tar.gz` and its sidecar bind
the same native commit and manifest. The archive supplies 32 authored composition
and release records, exact source custody, both graph carriers, and a portable
verifier. Check the sidecar, extract the archive, then run:

```sh
python3 -I -S -B stdo-v3.0.2-supplement/supplement.py verify \
  --bundle stdo-v3.0.2-supplement
```

Independent source and local-native readbacks passed. The exact manager wheel
passed 121 affected tests; a_c support passed 240 tests. Fresh isolated local
installation and both carrier recoveries passed on these exact assets. The
supplement is bounded to the selected 32 records; it does not complete the earlier
whole-method representation. Whole-method practical qualification, host behavior
and cost/efficiency claims remain outside this release's established evidence.

body":"# STDO 3.0.2

STDO 3.0.2 is a published immutable release with no RC suffix. It adds recursive
Product composition, explicit edge authority and context conditions, composition
contracts and examples, and source-matched reference frames. The stable-v1 release
profile gives this exact version an immutable tag while preserving historical
RC release and selector semantics.

The accompanying manager 0.1.6 wheel supports stable acquisition and explicit
composition-edge verification. The updated a_c and Codex/Claude Skills sources are
checkpointed on main; those independently owned tools and their consumer bases
retain their own lifecycle. Installing the native method does not adopt a project
or change an existing method installation.

## Exact release

| Coordinate | Identity |
|---|---|
| Immutable tag | `specification_methodology/v3.0.2` |
| Native commit C | `23ca9c0929d7be8570edafaf30542e3daeb8dc1f` |
| Annotated tag object T | `d03b00a7fdf8972dc236b52eb09f3eccba7f62cb` |
| Native manifest SHA256 | `f7f3f824ee1ac3e048d1b1ea86ce3aae84866e2e9d5010fe5eda2e38e12f4477` |

| Reviewed source A | `44448b14ecc9c5636d0e7972c7a4f1a80a07c623` |

The native distribution contains 86 payload files plus its installed manifest:
standards, generated frames, the supplied spec plugin, licence and release note.
The native predecessor is the published 3.0.1 RC1 commit; its tags and bytes remain
unchanged. No legacy 2.* coordinated cohort is republished.

## Install the exact method

Use Python 3.11 or later. Download the manager wheel, native manifest and their
checksum sidecars from the assets below. In that download directory, verify and create a separate environment:

```sh
shasum -a 256 -c stdo_toolchain-0.1.6-py3-none-any.whl.sha256
shasum -a 256 -c stdo-v3.0.2-manifest.json.sha256
python3 -m venv .stdo302
.stdo302/bin/python -I -m pip install ./stdo_toolchain-0.1.6-py3-none-any.whl
.stdo302/bin/python -I -m stdo_toolchain.cli --store ./stdo-store install v3.0.2 \
  --repository https://github.com/foolishimp/specification_methodology.git \
  --manifest-sha256 f7f3f824ee1ac3e048d1b1ea86ce3aae84866e2e9d5010fe5eda2e38e12f4477
.stdo302/bin/python -I -m stdo_toolchain.cli --store ./stdo-store verify v3.0.2 \
  --manifest-sha256 f7f3f824ee1ac3e048d1b1ea86ce3aae84866e2e9d5010fe5eda2e38e12f4477
```

The manager wheel is a separate distribution asset, not executable content added
to the native standards package. Existing installed 3.0.1/2.5.1 and pinned project
bases remain unchanged by this separate-store installation.

## Representation and evidence

The separate `stdo-v3.0.2-composition-release-supplement.tar.gz` and its sidecar bind
the same native commit and manifest. The archive supplies 32 authored composition
and release records, exact source custody, both graph carriers, and a portable
verifier. Check the sidecar, extract the archive, then run:

```sh
python3 -I -S -B stdo-v3.0.2-supplement/supplement.py verify \
  --bundle stdo-v3.0.2-supplement
```

Independent source and local-native readbacks passed. The exact manager wheel
passed 121 affected tests; a_c support passed 240 tests. Fresh isolated local
installation and both carrier recoveries passed on these exact assets. The
supplement is bounded to the selected 32 records; it does not complete the earlier
whole-method representation. Whole-method practical qualification, host behavior
and cost/efficiency claims remain outside this release's established evidence.
